original_card.question: Can one specified masked or overcomplete decoder improve the complete moment budget?
methods: Synthesize a decoder with exact coefficients and fully priced helper endpoints.
Bound the best possible budget for a fixed support alphabet before synthesis.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound and count all copied information, frames and restoration.

first_step.inspect: Locate the excluded classes: masked identities, at least nine terms, and deeper punctures.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one finite support alphabet and test exact decoding constraints before building a whole network.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A cheaper fully realized decoder could increase deficit or lower recursive cost on the binding complex side.
allowed_variations: Select a specific masked or overcomplete family with exact labels and supports.
scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: On the 112-line complement of the coordinate frame F = {e_{2a} ± e_{2a+1} : a = 0,1,2,3}, does any complex bilinear Gram ρ^T M σ that matches 2<ρ, σ> on even inner products differ from M = 2I, and do the odd pairs then still require cost-0 repairs?
scope_change_reason: The card allows one masked family with exact labels and supports. The family is geometric normal evaluations on this single P112 complement. Odd exactness is the dropped hypothesis. Non-geometric coefficients and nine-column factorizations are not claimed, and the eight-term all-pairs search is not repeated.
bottleneck_link: The binding complex supplier is priced from a decoder constant on a 112-port puncture. A geometric mask that produced a different M, or that required odd repairs with positive copied information, could change that constant. This family produces neither, so the mask alone does not improve the moment.
stop_rule: Stop once the even bilinear system on this P112 complement is solved and the odd-repair count is known. Do not search non-geometric supports or build a network in this session.
evidence: PASS_GEOMETRIC_MASKED_P112_REDUNDANCY proof_equations=108 proof_rank=64 live=112 even_live=6720 odd_live=5824 repairs=0 full_even_rank_mod=64 controls=2. The unique Gram is 2I, so eight-column geometric decoders are all-pairs decoders and the 5824 odd live pairs need no repair.

open_questions.question: Can nine or more columns factoring this same M = 2I have total label-pairing cost below the eight-column floor on this P112 set?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The redundancy result forces eight-column geometric masks back into the all-pairs theorem. An overcomplete factorization of the same Gram is the remaining geometric way to change copied information.
open_questions.first_step: Price one explicit nine-column factorization of 2I, with exact supports, including the repeated column.
open_questions.blocked_by: Support cost is not a function of M alone. Abstract nine-term floors in the discussion record are not this geometric factorization and are not replayed here.

open_questions.question: Which punctures make the even bilinear system have a positive-dimensional solution space?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A nontrivial M would be the first geometric mask that is not an all-pairs decoder and could change supports.
open_questions.first_step: Delete one further orbit of coordinate lines and rerun the 64-column rank on the even equations.
open_questions.blocked_by: A kernel matrix still needs supports, frames, and restoration before it is a budget. This package stops at the rigid P112 complement.
